events.title: Westminster Abbey Is Consecrated
events.description: Westminster Abbey, founded by King Edward the Confessor as England's first Romanesque church, was consecrated. It was a landmark of English church building.
events.significance: The abbey went on to host the coronations of English and British monarchs and became one of the country's most important national landmarks.

events.title: Iowa Joins the Union
events.description: Iowa was admitted to the United States as the 29th state. Its entry came during a period of rapid westward expansion.
events.significance: Iowa's admission extended the nation's boundaries further across the Midwest and strengthened the country's agricultural base.

events.title: Birth of Woodrow Wilson
events.description: Thomas Woodrow Wilson, the future 28th President of the United States, was born in Staunton, Virginia.
events.significance: Wilson led the United States through World War I and championed the creation of the League of Nations. His legacy remains widely debated.

events.title: The Lumière Brothers Premiere Cinema to a Paying Audience
events.description: In Paris, Auguste and Louis Lumière used their cinématographe to show motion pictures to a paying public for the first time.
events.significance: This screening is widely regarded as the birth of commercial cinema, and it launched the movie industry.

events.title: Muriel Siebert Breaks Wall Street's Glass Ceiling
events.description: Businesswoman Muriel Siebert became the first woman to own a seat on the New York Stock Exchange.
events.significance: Her achievement opened doors for women in finance and became a symbol of progress toward gender equality in the industry.
